title: Swift payroll salary structure
description: The components of a payslip and everything they read. See docs/data-format.md. The engine checks more than this schema can (references, cycles, unique names across inputs, constants and components, bracket tables); a structure that passes the schema can still be refused by Compiled::new.

$schema.description: A JSON Schema reference for editors; ignored by the engine.

id.description: Which structure this is; copied onto each payslip.

version.description: Which version of it; copied onto each payslip.

currency.description: The currency of every amount; copied onto each payslip.

rounding.description: How lines and totals are rounded. Defaults to two digits, half_up.

precision.description: round: a result needing more than 28 digits (1 / 3) is rounded far below a cent. exact: such a result is an error.

negative_net.description: What happens when deductions exceed gross pay. zero takes deductions in priority order and reports the rest as shortfall.

constants.description: Fixed figures and tables (bands, rates) that formulas read by name.

name.description: A lower-case ASCII letter or _, then lower-case letters, digits and _. Inputs, constants and components share one namespace.

decimal.description: A number, or decimal text such as "1500.50" (always read exactly).

mode.description: half_up: ties away from zero. half_even: ties to even. down: towards zero. up: away from zero.

default.description: Used when a person has no value; without one the input is required.

type.description: Checked when a person is read. number accepts a JSON number or decimal text.

id.description: The name formulas use for it.

formula.description: An expression in the swift_payroll_expr language.

input.description: The name of a declared input holding the amount.

when.description: A boolean condition; when false the line is zero and not applied.

tags.description: Groups for total("tag"). The kind is always an implicit tag.

priority.description: For a deduction under negative_net zero: lower numbers are taken from pay first; deductions without one come last, in listed order.
